title: Trigonometric Ratios — SOH-CAH-TOA, Your New Best Friends! 📐
hook: How do engineers measure the height of a mountain without climbing it? How do astronomers calculate distances to stars? They use trigonometry — the study of relationships between angles and sides of triangles. And it all starts with three simple ratios!
explanation:
In a right triangle with angle θ:
🔵 sin θ = Opposite / Hypotenuse = O/H
🟢 cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse = A/H
🟠 tan θ = Opposite / Adjacent = O/A
MEMORY TRICK
SOH — CAH — TOA   (Sin=O/H, Cos=A/H, Tan=O/A)
The reciprocal ratios:
RatioFormulaReciprocal of
cosec θH/O = 1/sin θsin θ
sec θH/A = 1/cos θcos θ
cot θA/O = 1/tan θtan θ
💡 Tip: The ratios depend ONLY on the angle θ, not on the size of the triangle! A bigger similar triangle gives the same ratios.
worked_example:
In a right triangle, if sin A = 3/5, find all other trig ratios:
1
From sin A = 3/5
Opposite = 3, Hypotenuse = 5 (or any multiple like 6/10)
2
Find Adjacent using Pythagoras
Adjacent = √(5² − 3²) = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4
3
Calculate all ratios
cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4
cosec A = 5/3, sec A = 5/4, cot A = 4/3
Triangle: sides 3, 4, 5 — a Pythagorean triplet! 🎯

try_this.question: In a right triangle ABC with ∠B = 90°, AB = 7 cm and AC = 25 cm. Find sin A, cos A, and tan A.
try_this.hint: First find BC using Pythagoras: BC = √(AC² − AB²). Then identify which side is opposite and which is adjacent to angle A.
try_this.answer:
BC = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm
For angle A: Opposite = BC = 24, Adjacent = AB = 7, Hypotenuse = AC = 25
sin A = 24/25, cos A = 7/25, tan A = 24/7

fun_fact: The word 'sine' comes from the Sanskrit word 'jyā' (meaning 'bowstring'), which was translated to Arabic as 'jiba', misread as 'jaib' (meaning 'bay/fold'), and then translated to Latin as 'sinus'! So every time you write 'sin', you're using a word with roots in ancient India! 🇮🇳
